key_insight: Gaussian process PDE solvers can incorporate linear inequality constraints by conditioning on them after the equality-based physics update, yielding a valid non-Gaussian posterior.
engineering_relevance: This lets engineers enforce admissibility such as nonnegativity, monotonicity, and no-arbitrage directly in probabilistic PDE models without changing the core solver.
method: Condition a GP prior on PDE residuals, boundary data, and measurements to obtain the physics-informed posterior.
Use that posterior as the prior for a finite-dimensional linear inequality event at virtual points.
Compute the resulting truncated-Gaussian moments to form the constrained posterior and diagnostics.
evidence_signal: Across Poisson, option-pricing, and air-quality experiments, constraints improved key metrics, including a 63% Poisson error reduction, 22% lower option extrapolation error, and a 74% drop in sub-zero-tail proxy.
watch_item: The inequality update is only finite-dimensional and relies on virtual points, so constraint placement and scalability may affect performance.
paper_title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
